---
title: "TA Guide: Helping with Setup"
toc: true
---

This page is for teaching assistants. It covers the same steps as the
participant's [Get Started](getting-started.qmd) page, in the order to do them
when you're helping someone from scratch: the API key goes into GitHub
**before** the codespace is created. For each step it lists what to check on
the participant's screen and what usually goes wrong.

Let the participant drive their own keyboard where you can. They will repeat
some of these steps (opening the codespace, `/key`, `/usage`) on their own
later in the week.

## Find out where they are

Ask which step they reached, then jump to it:

| They say... | Go to |
|---|---|
| "I can't see the Use this template button" | [GitHub account](#ta-github) |
| "I don't have a repository" or "I'm not sure which repo is mine" | [Their own repository](#ta-repo) |
| "/claim doesn't work" or "I didn't get a key" | [Discord and the API key](#ta-claim) |
| "The codespace is still loading" or "R doesn't work" | [Launch the codespace](#ta-launch) |
| "VS Code won't open the codespace" | [Connect](#ta-connect), then the [browser fallback](#ta-browser) |
| "Pi says there's no API key" | [The secret](#ta-secret), then [restart and test](#ta-restart) |

## 1. GitHub account {#ta-github}

- [ ] They are **signed in** to GitHub in the browser (their avatar shows in
      the top-right corner of [github.com](https://github.com)).
- [ ] It is the account they mean to use all week. People with a work and a
      personal account sometimes sign in with the wrong one.
- [ ] They know their password. They will sign in again from VS Code.

::: {.callout-tip title="If the green buttons are missing"}
GitHub hides **"Use this template"** and **"Code"** from visitors who aren't
signed in. Missing buttons almost always mean the participant is signed out.
:::

If GitHub refuses to create a repository or a codespace on a brand-new
account, check that the account's email address is verified (GitHub's
settings page shows a banner when it isn't).

## 2. Their own repository {#ta-repo}

- [ ] They opened the
      [workshop 2 template](https://github.com/elsherbini/data-science-for-biology-nov2026-codespace)
      and chose **"Use this template" → "Create a new repository"**.
- [ ] The new repository's address is `github.com/THEIR-USERNAME/...`, not
      `github.com/elsherbini/...`. Read the URL bar to confirm.
- [ ] The page under the repository name says
      *"generated from elsherbini/data-science-for-biology-nov2026-codespace"*.

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistake: Open in a codespace"}
The **"Use this template"** dropdown also offers **"Open in a codespace"**.
That launches a codespace with no repository of their own behind it, so
they can't save work to GitHub and can't give the API key access to it. If
they did this, delete that codespace at
[github.com/codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces) and start again with
**"Create a new repository"**.
:::

Forks don't work either. If they see "forked from" under the repository name,
have them create a fresh repository from the template.

## 3. Discord and the API key {#ta-claim}

Before they type anything:

- [ ] They are in the **workshop server**, not in a direct message, and can
      see the
      [workshop channel](https://discord.com/channels/1567172556065079337/1567172557340278806).
      If not, send them the [invite](https://discord.gg/9a9WcAUMR).
- [ ] **You have given them the Participant role.** Ask for their Discord
      username and find them in the member list. Left-click their name,
      click **+ Add Role**, and choose **Participant**. If you don't see
      **+ Add Role**, your account can't assign roles yet; tell Joseph.

::: {.callout-important title="Role first, then /claim"}
The bot only gives keys to people with the Participant role. Without the
role, `/claim` does nothing: no reply, no error. If a participant says
"nothing happened", check the role, assign it, and have them run `/claim`
again.
:::

Then they type `/claim`:

- [ ] As they type, a pop-up shows the bot's `/claim` command. They pick it
      from the pop-up (or press Enter while it's highlighted).
- [ ] The reply says **"Only you can see this"** and contains a key starting
      with `sk-or-v1-`.
- [ ] They copy the **whole** key. Use the copy button if the reply has one,
      or select carefully from `sk-or` to the last character.

If they dismissed the reply or lost the key, `/key` shows it again. `/usage`
shows how much of today's budget they've spent; it resets at midnight UTC.

::: {.callout-caution title="Keys are personal"}
If a participant pastes their key into a public channel, ask them to delete
the message and tell Joseph so the key can be replaced. Don't photograph or
copy anyone's key yourself.
:::

## 4. Add the secret to GitHub {#ta-secret}

- [ ] They are on their **personal** Codespaces settings page:
      [github.com/settings/codespaces](https://github.com/settings/codespaces).
      A secret added under the repository's **Settings → Secrets and variables
      → Actions** does not reach the codespace.
- [ ] Under **"Codespace user secrets"** they clicked **"New secret"**.
- [ ] **Name** is exactly `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`: all capitals, underscores,
      no spaces. Check the spelling letter by letter; this is the most common
      fault.
- [ ] **Value** is the key from Discord, with no space or blank line before
      or after it.
- [ ] **Repository access** lists **their** repository from step 2. "Select
      repositories" and then picking the repo is easy to skip.
- [ ] They clicked **"Add secret"** and the secret now appears in the list.

To fix a typo in the value or the repository access, click **Update** next to
the secret. To fix a typo in the name, delete the secret and add a new one.

## 5. Launch the codespace {#ta-launch}

::: {.callout-important title="Secret saved? Then launch"}
A codespace reads its secrets only when it **starts**, so check that
[step 4](#ta-secret) is done before creating the codespace. If they already
have a codespace from before the secret existed (for example, built on
Monday), don't create another one: skip to [step 8](#ta-restart) and restart
it.
:::

- [ ] On **their own** repository: **"Code" → "Codespaces" tab →
      "Create codespace on main"**.
- [ ] Only **one** codespace for this repository. Check
      [github.com/codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces). If they clicked
      the button several times, delete the extras so they don't open the
      wrong one later. (Brand-new extras hold no work, so they're safe to
      delete. For older ones, see the warning in [step 6](#ta-connect).)
- [ ] Machine type is the default **2-core**. Bigger machines use up their
      free monthly Codespaces hours faster.
- [ ] The first build has finished. It takes 10 minutes or more. Closing the
      tab doesn't stop the build.

Check that R works: **Terminal → New Terminal**, type `R`, then
`library(tidyverse)`. A list of attached packages and no line starting with
`Error` means the build is good. `q("no")` leaves R.

::: {.callout-warning title="If the build failed"}
A message about **recovery mode**, or `R: command not found` in the terminal,
means the container didn't build. Open the Command Palette
(<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>P</kbd>, or
<kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>P</kbd> on a Mac) and run
**"Codespaces: Full Rebuild Container"**. If that fails too, delete the
codespace and create a new one, and tell Joseph.
:::

## 6. Connect from VS Code on their laptop {#ta-connect}

The codespace opens in a browser tab by default. We'd like participants to
use the VS Code desktop app, which handles keyboard shortcuts and copy-paste
better than the browser.

- [ ] VS Code is installed on the laptop
      ([code.visualstudio.com/download](https://code.visualstudio.com/download)).
- [ ] They have launched the codespace at least once from GitHub
      ([step 5](#ta-launch)). VS Code can only connect to a codespace that
      already exists.

To connect:

1. In VS Code, click the icon in the **bottom-left corner** of the window
   (two small arrows).
2. Choose **"Connect to Codespace"**.
3. The first time, VS Code asks them to sign in to GitHub and authorize VS
   Code. This opens a browser page; they approve it there and return to
   VS Code.
4. Their codespace appears in the list. Click it.

::: {.callout-warning title="Connect, never Create"}
The same menu offers **"Create New Codespace"**. Tell the participant to
choose **"Connect to Codespace"** every time, today and every morning after.
Someone who picks Create gets a fresh, empty codespace, and their work ends
up split across several codespaces.

If a participant already has more than one, open
[github.com/codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces) and work out which one
holds their work (usually the oldest). Before deleting any extra codespace,
open it and check the **Source Control** panel: if it lists changed files,
they commit and push them first. Deleting a codespace deletes anything in it
that wasn't pushed to GitHub.
:::

- [ ] The bottom-left corner of VS Code shows **Codespaces:** followed by the
      codespace's name. If it doesn't, the window is a local VS Code window,
      not the codespace.
- [ ] VS Code is signed in to the **same** GitHub account as the browser (the
      person icon at the bottom of the left-hand bar). If the codespace list
      is empty, this is usually why.

## 7. Fall back to the browser {#ta-browser}

If the desktop app won't connect after a couple of tries, don't spend the
session on it. VS Code in the browser is the same editor, and everything in
the workshop works there.

- [ ] At [github.com/codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces), click **⋯**
      next to the codespace and choose **"Open in" → "Open in browser"**.
- [ ] Use Chrome, Edge or Firefox. Safari has trouble pasting into the
      terminal.
- [ ] When the browser asks for clipboard permission, allow it. Without it,
      pasting into the terminal fails.

Some shortcuts belong to the browser instead of VS Code
(<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>W</kbd> closes the browser tab, for example). The
**Terminal**, **View** and other menus are in the ☰ menu at the top left.

If clicking the codespace's name tries to launch the desktop app when they
wanted the browser, their default is set to VS Code. They can change it under
**Editor preference** on the
[Codespaces settings page](https://github.com/settings/codespaces).

## 8. Restart and test {#ta-restart}

If the codespace was created **after** the secret was saved (the order on
this page), skip the first two checks and go straight to the test.

- [ ] At [github.com/codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces), **⋯ → "Stop
      codespace"**. Wait until it shows as stopped. Closing the tab or
      reloading the page is not enough.
- [ ] Open it again (desktop app or browser, as in step 6 or 7).
- [ ] In a new terminal, run:

  ```bash
  echo ${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:0:9}
  ```

  It should print `sk-or-v1-` and nothing else of the key. A blank line
  means the codespace can't see the secret: go back to
  [step 4](#ta-secret), check the name and the repository access, then
  restart again.
- [ ] Run `pi`. Pi starts and answers a short question such as
      "what files are in this folder?".

If Pi starts but every request fails with an error about credit or budget,
have them run `/usage` in Discord. If they haven't spent anything and it still
fails, tell Joseph.

## When to hand off

Pass it to Joseph or another instructor when:

- the container fails to build twice,
- the bot won't give a key to someone who has the Participant role,
- a key has been posted publicly,
- you have spent 15 minutes on one participant and the browser fallback
  hasn't helped.
